rows.value: UK residents under the Statutory Residence Test within their first 4 years of UK residence, after at least 10 consecutive years of non-residence

rows.label: Corporation Tax, with Domestic and Multinational Top-up Tax [national]
rows.value: 25% main rate, 19% small profits rate, Marginal Relief between £50,000 and £250,000; 15% minimum effective rate for groups with revenue over €750 million. Paid by UK resident companies and UK permanent establishments of non-UK companies. Legal basis: Corporation Tax Acts 2009 and 2010; Finance (No.2) Act 2023 Parts 3 and 4. In force: financial year from 1 April 2026; top-up taxes for accounting periods beginning on or after 31 December 2023

In force: IR35 reform from 6 April 2021; CIS no start date stated

rows.value: Cash basis by default; £1,000 trading allowance; flat-rate expenses (£0.55 a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in 2026-27). In force: cash basis default from 6 April 2024; trading allowance from 6 April 2017

rows.source_title: MHCLG: Council Tax levels set by local authorities in England 2026 to 2027: Technical Notes (published 25 March 2026)
rows.label: Council Tax (domestic property tax) [local]
rows.value: Band D amount set by each council, other bands a fixed fraction of it; England average Band D £2,392 in 2026-27; Northern Ireland has domestic rates instead. Paid by occupiers aged 18 or over (owners of empty or second homes). Legal basis: Council Tax replaced the community charge on 1 April 1993; referendum limits under the Localism Act 2011. In force: 2026-27 financial year, from 1 April 2026

rows.label: Business rates (non-domestic property tax) [local]
rows.value: England 2026-27: 43.2p to 50.8p per £1 of rateable value (retail, hospitality and leisure 38.2p and 43p); Scotland and Wales set their own multipliers. Paid by ratepayers of non-domestic property. Legal basis: Local Government Finance Act 1988 (Schedule 4ZA for the multipliers). In force: 2026-27 financial year, from 1 April 2026

rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Stamp Duty Land Tax (printable guide)
rows.label: Stamp Duty Land Tax (England and Northern Ireland) [national]
rows.value: 0% to 12% on residential bands; +5% for additional dwellings; +2% for non-UK residents; 17% for certain companies over £500,000; non-residential 0% to 5%. Paid by buyers of land and property. Legal basis: Finance Act 2003. In force: residential rates from 1 April 2025

rows.source_title: Revenue Scotland: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax: Residential property
rows.label: Property transfer tax: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (Scotland) [devolved: Scotland]
rows.value: 0% to 12% on residential bands; first-time buyer nil band £175,000; Additional Dwelling Supplement 8% of the price; non-residential 0% to 5%. Paid by buyers of land and property in Scotland. Legal basis: Land and Buildings Transaction Tax (Scotland) Act 2013. In force: residential rates from 1 April 2021; ADS rate from 5 December 2024

rows.source_title: Welsh Revenue Authority: Land Transaction Tax rates and bands (last updated 10 December 2024)
rows.label: Property transfer tax: Land Transaction Tax (Wales) [devolved: Wales]
rows.value: 0% to 12% on main residential bands; higher residential rates 5% to 17%; non-residential 0% to 6%. Paid by buyers of land and property in Wales. Legal basis: Welsh legislation; rates set by Welsh Ministers and approved by the Welsh Parliament; collected by the Welsh Revenue Authority. In force: replaced SDLT in Wales from 1 April 2018; main rates from 10 October 2022

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item A3
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Income Tax in Scotland: Current rates (2026 to 2027)
rows.label: Devolved regional income tax: Scottish Income Tax and Welsh rates of Income Tax [regional]
rows.value: Scotland 2026-27: 19% starter to 48% top rate on non-savings, non-dividend income; Wales: 20%, 40% and 45% (same bands as England); savings and dividends at UK rates. Paid by taxpayers who live in Scotland or Wales (collected by HMRC through PAYE and Self Assessment). Rates set by the Scottish Government and the Welsh Government; detailed tables on the Scotland and Wales nation pages.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item A5; detailed table: capital-gains
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Capital Gains Tax rates
rows.label: Capital Gains Tax [national]
rows.value: 18% within the basic rate band and 24% above it (from 6 April 2026); 18% with Business Asset Disposal Relief; Annual Exempt Amount £3,000 (£1,500 for trusts). Paid by individuals, trustees and personal representatives. Taxation of Chargeable Gains Act 1992.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item A6; detailed table: withholding-investment
rows.source_title: HMRC internal manual SAIM9010: Deduction of tax: introduction
rows.label: Withholding on interest and royalties (deduction of income tax at source) [national]
rows.value: Income tax at the basic rate deducted from yearly interest and from patent royalties and other qualifying annual payments; no deduction by banks and building societies on deposit interest since 6 April 2016. Paid by recipients (deducted by the payer). Income Tax Act 2007 Part 15.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item A7; detailed table: rental-income
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Renting out your property: Paying tax and National Insurance
rows.label: Rental income and pension income [national]
rows.value: Taxed at the Income Tax rates; first £1,000 of property income tax-free (property allowance); non-resident landlords: basic rate deducted from rent by agents and tenants; pensions taxed as income, up to 25% of a pension (at most £268,275) tax-free as a lump sum. Paid by landlords and pensioners. Income Tax (Trading and Other Income) Act 2005; Non-resident Landlord Scheme.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item C2; detailed table: property-tax-business-rates
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Estimate your business rates (multipliers for the 2026 to 2027 tax year)
rows.label: Local business tax: business rates on non-domestic property [municipal]
rows.value: Rateable value times a multiplier; England 2026-27: 43.2p to 50.8p per £1 (retail, hospitality and leisure 38.2p and 43p); Scotland and Wales set their own. Paid by occupiers of non-domestic property. Local Government Finance Act 1988; detailed table in the business rates section.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item D3; detailed table: excise
rows.source_title: HMRC: Alcohol Duty rates (last updated 1 February 2026)
rows.label: Excise duties: alcohol, tobacco, fuel and the Soft Drinks Industry Levy [national]
rows.value: Alcohol £9.96 to £33.99 per litre of pure alcohol by strength (from 1 February 2026); cigarettes 16.5% of retail price plus £394.09 per 1,000 (minimum £518.75) from 1 October 2026; petrol and diesel 52.95p per litre; soft drinks £2.08 or £2.78 per 10 litres. Paid by producers and importers (passed on in prices). Finance (No. 2) Act 2023 (Alcohol Duty); Tobacco Products Duty Act 1979; Hydrocarbon Oil Duties Act 1979; Finance Act 2017 (Soft Drinks Industry Levy).

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item D4; detailed table: insurance-premium-tax
rows.source_title: HMRC: Insurance Premium Tax: guide for insurers (last updated 6 March 2019)
rows.label: Insurance Premium Tax [national]
rows.value: 12% standard rate; 20% higher rate (travel insurance and some insurance sold with appliances or vehicles); most long-term insurance exempt. Paid by insurers (passed on in premiums). Finance Act 1994 Part III.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item D4; detailed table: financial-transaction-tax
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Tax when you buy shares
rows.label: Stamp Duty and Stamp Duty Reserve Tax on share purchases (financial transaction tax) [national]
rows.value: 0.5% of the price (Stamp Duty on stock transfer forms over £1,000; SDRT on electronic purchases); 1.5% into some depositary receipt schemes or clearance services. Paid by buyers of shares. Finance Act 1986 (SDRT); Stamp Act 1891.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item D4; detailed table: digital-services-tax
rows.source_title: HM Treasury and HMRC policy paper: Digital Services Tax (published 11 March 2020)
rows.label: Digital Services Tax [national]
rows.value: 2% of UK-user revenues above a £25 million allowance, for groups with over £500 million worldwide digital revenues and over £25 million from UK users. Paid by groups providing search engines, social media services and online marketplaces. Finance Act 2020 Part 2.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item D5; detailed table: energy-tax
rows.source_title: HMRC: Climate Change Levy rates (last updated 17 November 2026)
rows.label: Climate Change Levy (energy tax on business energy use) [national]
rows.value: Main rates from 1 April 2026: £0.00801 per kWh of electricity or gas, £0.02175 per kg of LPG; Carbon Price Support rates for electricity generators. Paid by business energy users (charged by suppliers); generators for the Carbon Price Support rates. Finance Act 2000 Schedule 6.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item E4; detailed table: inheritance
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: How Inheritance Tax works: thresholds, rules and allowances
rows.label: Inheritance Tax [national]
rows.value: 40% above the £325,000 nil-rate band (residence nil-rate band up to £175,000 more for a home left to direct descendants, estates under £2 million); 36% if 10% or more goes to charity; gifts within 7 years of death taxed with taper relief. Paid by estates (paid by executors); recipients of lifetime gifts in some cases. Inheritance Tax Act 1984.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item F1; detailed table: vehicle-taxes
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Vehicle tax rates: Cars registered on or after 1 April 2017
rows.label: Vehicle tax (Vehicle Excise Duty) [national]
rows.value: First-year rate by CO2 emissions, £10 to £5,690 (cars from 1 April 2017); then £200 a year; £440 a year extra for 5 years on cars over £40,000 (electric over £50,000). Paid by vehicle keepers. Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item F2; detailed table: environmental-tax
rows.source_title: HMRC: Plastic Packaging Tax: steps to take (last updated 12 February 2026)
rows.label: Environmental taxes: Plastic Packaging Tax, Landfill Tax and Aggregates Levy [national]
rows.value: Plastic Packaging Tax £228.82 per tonne (under 30% recycled plastic); Landfill Tax £130.75 per tonne (lower rate £8.65); Aggregates Levy £2.16 per tonne (all from 1 April 2026). Paid by manufacturers and importers of plastic packaging, landfill operators, aggregate producers. Finance Act 2021 Part 2 (Plastic Packaging Tax); Finance Act 1996 Part III (Landfill Tax); Finance Act 2001 Part 2 (Aggregates Levy).

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item F3
rows.source_title: City of Edinburgh Council: About the Edinburgh Visitor Levy
rows.label: Tourist tax: visitor levies on overnight stays (Edinburgh, Wales) [municipal]
rows.value: Edinburgh Visitor Levy 5% of the accommodation cost for the first 5 nights, for stays from 24 July 2026; Wales Visitor Levy £1.30 (75p in hostels and on campsites) per person per night where a council adopts it, Cardiff from 1 April 2027. Paid by overnight visitors (collected by accommodation providers). Visitor Levy (Scotland) Act 2024; Visitor Accommodation (Register and Levy) Etc. (Wales) Act 2025.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item F4; detailed table: air-passenger-tax
rows.source_title: HMRC: Rates for Air Passenger Duty (last updated 1 April 2026)
rows.label: Air Passenger Duty [national]
rows.value: Per passenger from 1 April 2026: £8 to £142 domestic, £15 to £142 band A, £102 to £1,097 band B, £106 to £1,141 band C (reduced, standard and higher rates). Paid by aircraft operators (passed on in fares). Finance Act 1994 Part I Chapter IV.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item G1; detailed table: customs
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Tax and customs for goods sent from abroad: Tax and duty
rows.label: Customs duty, import VAT and traveller allowances [national]
rows.value: No customs duty on non-excise goods of £135 or less (VAT collected by the seller); above £135, duty by the Trade Tariff on price plus postage and insurance, and import VAT; traveller allowance £390 of goods (£270 by private plane or boat); cash of £10,000 or more must be declared. Paid by importers and travellers. Taxation (Cross-border Trade) Act 2018; Value Added Tax Act 1994.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item H1; detailed table: financial-transaction-tax
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: Tax when you buy shares
rows.label: Stamp duty on documents: stock transfer forms [national]
rows.value: 0.5% on share transfers made with a stock transfer form, when the transaction is over £1,000. Paid by buyers. Stamp Act 1891 and Finance Act 1986.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item H2; detailed table: tv-licence
rows.source_title: GOV.UK: TV Licence
rows.label: TV Licence (broadcasting licence fee) [national]
rows.value: £180 a year (£60.50 for black and white sets), for homes and businesses that watch or record live TV or use BBC iPlayer. Paid by households and businesses. Communications Act 2003 Part 4.

rows.section: Complete list of taxes, levies and charges
rows.note: Checklist item H3; detailed table: inbound-regime
rows.source_title: HMRC: Check if you can claim the 4-year foreign income and gains regime (published 6 April 2025)
rows.label: New residents: 4-year foreign income and gains regime (expat regime) [national]
rows.value: No UK tax on eligible foreign income and gains for the first 4 years of UK residence after 10 years of non-residence; replaced the remittance basis on 6 April 2025; foreign earnings excluded (Overseas Workday Relief instead). Paid by qualifying new UK residents (claimed on the Self Assessment return). Finance Act 2025.
